- **Record lines** are the record's text split on `\n`, with one `\r` directly before each `\n` removed.
- **A section** of a record is the lines after a line equal to `## <name>` up to the next line starting `## `.
- **The trigger text** of an ADR is taken from the first line in its `Consequences` section that starts `**Revisit if:**` or `- **Revisit if:**`. Take the rest of that line, with one trailing HTML comment and surrounding whitespace removed.
  - When that rest is not empty, the trigger text is it, followed by each next line up to the first blank line or line starting `#`, `- **` or `**`.
  - When it is empty and the next line is blank, the trigger text is the lines after that blank line that start `- `, or start with a space or tab and are not blank, up to the first line that is neither.

Matches are taken left to right; where several start at the same place the longest wins, and a match that overlaps an earlier one is not taken, so `5 October 2026` is one mention.   - `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real calendar date: that day;
  - `YYYY-MM`, month 01 to 12: the last day of that month;
  - `<Month> D, YYYY` or `D <Month> YYYY`, with `<Month>` an English month name with a capital first letter, a real calendar date: that day;
  - `<Month> YYYY`: the last day of that month;
  - `Q1 YYYY` to `Q4 YYYY`: the last day of that quarter;
  - a bare year from `1900` to `2099`: 31 December of that year.

- **A version mention** in a text is a match of either form:
  - optionally one of `v`, `>=`, `<=`, `==`, `~=` or `^`, then two or more dot-separated digit runs, then an optional `+`, not preceded by a letter, digit, `_`, `.` or `-` and not followed by more letters or digits joined to it by `.`, `_` or `-`;
  - `v` followed by digits, not preceded by a letter, digit, `_`, `.` or `-` and not followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.`.

  1. `due`: its trigger text holds a date mention that has passed;
  2. `version`: it holds a version mention;
  3. `scheduled`: it holds a date mention;
  4. `stable`: its trigger text, with one pair of wrapping backticks removed and casefolded, is `stable`, or starts with `stable` followed by a space, `—`, `-` or `:`;

- **A header citation** of a superseded ADR S by an accepted record R is a match of S's identifier as a whole word in R's header, where all of these hold:
  - R is not S and is not one of S's successors;
  - the match is not in R's `Supersedes` or `Supersedes in part` field;
  - R's header names none of S's successors as a whole word.
- **The signal text** of an accepted ADR is, for each line in its `Confirmation` section that starts with `**Signal`, `- **Signal` or the same after spaces, that line and the lines after it up to the next line, after leading spaces and a `- ` are removed, that starts `**Mode`, `**Signal` or `**Owner`.
- **A URI scheme** is, at the start of a text, an ASCII letter followed by one or more ASCII letters, digits, `+`, `-` or `.`, then `:`. A single letter before `:` is a drive letter, not a scheme.
- **A path candidate** comes from a backtick span or a Markdown link target in signal text:
  - a backtick span is the text between a pair of single backticks on one line. Remove a trailing `::` and everything after it, then a trailing `:` followed by digits, optionally `-` and digits. What is left is skipped when it starts with a URI scheme, so `cli.py:247` yields `cli.py` and `https://example.com/x` is skipped;
  - a link target is the text in `](…)` up to its first space. Targets that start with a URI scheme and targets starting `#` are skipped. Remove a `#` or `?` and everything after it;

For a link target, it is the target lexically joined to the ADR's directory and normalised, so `..` segments are resolved; a target that does not start with `/` and whose normalised form leaves the repository root is invalid.
- **A rooted candidate** is one that is invalid, or whose checked form's first `/`-separated segment equals the name of an entry directly under the repository root. A candidate that is not rooted is **unlocated**.
- **A signal item** is one ADR and one checked form: candidates with the same ADR and checked form are one item. Every count and list of candidates in the health result is of signal items, except where AC-0025 counts occurrences. A signal item is reported by its checked form, cleaned.
- **The lexical rule:** a candidate is invalid when its checked form starts with `/`, `~` or a drive letter and `:`, holds `\`, a NUL or any character of Unicode category `Cc`, `Cf`, `Zl`, `Zp`, `Co` or `Cs`, has a `.` or `..` segment, is longer than 160 code points, or has more than 32 `/`-separated segments.   - `invalid`: it fails the lexical rule; or a component on its path is a symbolic link, a reparse point, or neither a regular file nor a directory; or its last component is a regular file with more than one hard link; or inspecting a component fails for any reason other than "does not exist", or the confinement helper refuses a directory on its path;

## Context

RFC-0044 / ADR-0034 grounded the downstream *build* loop in the platform's real contract and runtime truth. But the design phase that sits **between** them still reasons from model memory: the routing axis is in place, yet the serverless lens it would route to was deferred (ADR-0032's scope-boundary call, RFC-0042 D5), and **no discipline forces a binding-platform fact into view for any managed service** at design time.

29	Two independent, multi-day builds on *different* AWS stacks (`docs/rfc/0045-notes/field-report.md`) falsify the implicit assumption that abstract pillars are enough at design altitude. 30	
31	1. **The structurally-fatal latency miss (an agent system).** The design modelled a 30–60 s multi-round LLM-agent turn as a *fully synchronous, blocking* request behind a managed HTTP API with a **non-configurable ~29 s integration timeout**, and explicitly dismissed the async alternative as "over-engineered for a real-time agent." 33	
34	The unifying cause matches RFC-0044's, **one inner-loop stage earlier**: the design is shaped, and reviewed, against model memory and abstract pillars rather than the platform's **binding contract** — but at a stage where **nothing is deployed and no toolchain oracle can be run**. - **Applies to:** the `product-engineering` pack's discovery capability and every downstream consumer that reads the produced sidecar instances (the traceability lint, `work-loop`, the release loop).
- **Tradeoff accepted:** the controller scheduling the recursive walk in-context is a **bet on a shallow tree**, gated by depth/breadth bounds; scheduling many concurrent/parked threads stays the harness's job.
- **Revisit if:** a real recursive walk shows in-context scheduling does not hold at depth, or an adopter harness cannot supply the agent-untokened verdict channel the security contract requires.

## Context

RFC-0048's operating model needs an **upstream** loop that turns a raw idea into a build-ready brief — the peer of `work-loop`'s downstream spec→build loop. The open question (D7/D8) was *how much machinery* to ship: a from-scratch coordinator runtime (an engine that schedules lenses, solves convergence, and drives a state machine), or content the existing harness runs.

The Decision-7 spike walked the worked example G0→G2 as **one reasoning context**, with the two named failure modes (over-scope; an unbacked security-sensitive screen) deliberately injected. Every transition was a **file edit plus, at most, the connectedness lint**. The riskiest assumption — that orchestrating the loop needs a runtime engine — was **refuted**. The recursion pressure-test (does a nested plan-tree force a state-machine engine?) found research *strengthens* the no-engine claim: Hierarchical-Task-Network planning over a blackboard is a plan tree held as **data**, walked by one controller — the opposite choice (a nested finite-state machine) is what fails to scale.

This ADR records the load-bearing, expensive-to-reverse calls — the **form**, the **home**, and the **no-engine line** — so a future maintainer does not re-litigate them. The mechanical detail (the slot field-sets, the gate state machine, the verdict set, the security ACs) is spec-level and lives in the `discovery-loop` implementing spec and the carried schema reference, not here.

Constraints in force when deciding:

- **Principle 3 (a habit, not infrastructure).** The repo ships doctrine and prose the agent reasons from, never a runtime engine, daemon, scheduler, or wrapper. This is the bar that put browser-bridge out of charter.
- **Principle 2 (no duplication).** The sidecar schema lives in exactly one place; no parallel `core` copy and no duplicated prose in `work-loop`.
- **Principle 1 (universal / portable).** The contract is harness-neutral — it must run in whatever harness the adopter uses, including a non-repo store (an Obsidian vault), which is why the schema is carried in the producer pack, not repo-scope `core`.
- **The reviewer ceiling (ADR-0042, superseding ADR-0023).** Agent additions are keyed to loop + work type; the discovery roster is loop-scoped and admitted under that policy, while the core code-review ceiling stays three lenses.
